breadcrumb: Std 9 Social Science (English) — Geography Unit 5: Biosphere — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: The vertical range of the biosphere is approximately 20 km, ... most plants and animals live in a very narrow section for about 1 km above and below the Mean Sea Level (MSL).

en.q: The vertical range of the biosphere is approximately
en.explanation: It is measured from the ocean floor to the troposphere; most life lives about 1 km above and below mean sea level.

ta.explanation: கடல்தளம் முதல் கீழடுக்கு வரை இது அளக்கப்படுகிறது.

questions.quote: An ecosystem consists of three basic components: A) Abiotic components B) Biotic components and C) Energy component

en.q: The three basic components of an ecosystem are
options: trophic, food chain and food web
en.explanation: Producers, consumers and decomposers are the biotic components.

options: ஆற்றல் மட்டம், உணவுச் சங்கிலி, உணவு வலை
ta.explanation: உற்பத்தியாளர், நுகர்வோர், சிதைப்போர் ஆகியோர் உயிரியல் கூறுகள்.

questions.quote: Primary consumers ... exclusively herbivores. Eg. zebra, goat. Secondary consumers are small carnivores... Eg. lion, snake. Tertiary consumers are top carnivores ... Eg. owl, crocodile

en.q:
Match List I with List II.
List I: a) Producers  b) Primary consumers  c) Secondary consumers  d) Decomposers
List II: 1) Fungi, mushrooms  2) Plants, algae  3) Zebra, goat  4) Snake, lion (per the textbook)
en.explanation: Producers are autotrophs; primary consumers are herbivores; secondary consumers eat herbivores; decomposers are saprotrophs.

ta.q:
பட்டியல் I-ஐ பட்டியல் II உடன் பொருத்துக.
பட்டியல் I: அ) உற்பத்தியாளர்கள்  ஆ) முதல்நிலை நுகர்வோர்  இ) இரண்டாம்நிலை நுகர்வோர்  ஈ) சிதைப்போர்
பட்டியல் II: 1) பூஞ்சை, காளான்  2) தாவரங்கள், பாசிகள்  3) வரிக்குதிரை, ஆடு  4) பாம்பு, சிங்கம் (நூலின்படி)
ta.explanation: உற்பத்தியாளர் - தாவரங்கள்; முதல்நிலை நுகர்வோர் - தாவர உண்ணிகள்; சிதைப்போர் - பூஞ்சை.

questions.quote: Biomes are defined by abiotic factors like relief, climate, soils and vegetation. They are classified into two broad categories, terrestrial biomes and aquatic biomes. Terrestrial biomes are mainly determined by temperature and rainfall.

en.q: Terrestrial biomes are mainly determined by
en.explanation: Aquatic biomes are classified as freshwater and marine.

ta.q: நிலவாழ் பல்லுயிர்த் தொகுதிகள் முதன்மையாக எவற்றால் தீர்மானிக்கப்படுகின்றன?
ta.explanation: நீர்வாழ் தொகுதிகள் நன்னீர், கடல் என இருவகை.

questions.quote: An ecological region that has lost more than 70% of its original habitat is considered a hotspot. Hotspots in India are the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo Burma Region and Sundaland. There are 34 areas around the world which are qualified as biodiversity hotspots

en.q: How many biodiversity hotspots does the textbook say exist around the world?
en.explanation: A region that has lost more than 70% of its original habitat is a hotspot. (The textbook lists the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma and Sundaland as India's hotspots; Sundaland covers the Nicobar Islands.)

ta.q: உலகில் உயிரினப் பன்மை வளமையங்கள் எத்தனை எனப் பாடநூல் கூறுகிறது?
ta.explanation: அசல் வாழிடத்தில் 70%க்கு மேல் இழந்த பகுதி வளமையம் எனப்படும்.

questions.quote: Hotspots in India are the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo Burma Region and Sundaland.

en.q: Which of the following is an Indian biodiversity hotspot named in the textbook?
en.explanation: The others are the Himalayas, Indo-Burma and Sundaland.

ta.q: நூலில் குறிப்பிடப்பட்ட இந்திய உயிரினப் பன்மை வளமையம் எது?

questions.quote: The U.S. National Cancer Institute has identified about 70% of the plants used for treating cancer which are found only in rain forests. Eg. Lapacho.

en.q: According to the textbook, the U.S. National Cancer Institute identified what share of anti-cancer plants as found only in rain forests?

ta.q: புற்றுநோய் சிகிச்சைக்கான தாவரங்களில் எத்தனை சதவிகிதம் மழைக்காடுகளில் மட்டுமே உள்ளன என அமெரிக்கத் தேசிய புற்றுநோய் நிறுவனம் அடையாளம் கண்டது (நூலின்படி)?

questions.quote: Tropical grasslands are generally found between tropical forests and deserts... flat and are found in the Sahel, south of Sahara in East Africa and in Australia... The grass which grow here are tall and sharp. Hence the chief occupation of the people is herding.

en.q: The chief occupation of people in tropical savanna biomes is
en.explanation: The primitive people living there are nomadic.

questions.quote: Deserts are usually found on the western margins of the continents between 20° and 30° North and South latitudes. The annual rainfall is less than 25 cm. An oasis is a fertile fresh water source found in deserts.

en.q: Deserts are usually found on the western margins of continents between
en.explanation: Annual rainfall in deserts is less than 25 cm; oases support date palms, figs, citrus fruits and maize.

ta.q: பாலைவனங்கள் கண்டங்களின் மேற்கு விளிம்புகளில் காணப்படும் அட்சங்கள்

questions.quote: An oasis is a fertile fresh water source found in deserts and semi-arid regions. Oases are fed by springs. Crops like date palms, figs, citrus fruits, maize etc. are cultivated near these oases.

en.q: A fertile fresh water source in deserts, fed by springs, where date palms are grown, is called an
en.explanation: Date palms, figs, citrus fruits and maize are cultivated.

ta.q: பாலைவனத்தில் ஊற்றுகளால் நிரம்பி பேரீச்சை விளையும் வளமான நன்னீர் இடம்
ta.explanation: பாலைவனச் சோலைகளில் பேரீச்சை, அத்தி, சிட்ரஸ் பயிரிடப்படுகின்றன.

questions.quote: Temperate Grasslands are usually found in the interior of the continents... These regions favour wheat cultivation. Extensive mechanised agriculture is practised due to lack of farm labour.

options: in continental interiors, good for wheat
in the polar regions near the poles
in the hot equatorial rainforest region
on the western margins of continents
en.explanation: They have large seasonal temperature variations; pastoral industry is the main occupation.

questions.quote: Temperate grasslands: Prairies - North America; Steppes - Eurasia; Pampas - Argentina and Uruguay; Veld - South Africa; Downs - Australia; Canterbury - New Zealand

en.q:
Match List I with List II.
List I: a) Prairies  b) Steppes  c) Pampas  d) Veld
List II: 1) South Africa  2) Eurasia  3) North America  4) Argentina and Uruguay
en.explanation: Downs are in Australia and Canterbury in New Zealand.

questions.quote: Tundra Biomes ... Greenland, Arctic and Antarctic regions ... also called Barren lands... They live in igloos in winter and in tents during summer. Arctic moss, Arctic willow, lichens... polar bear, wolverine, reindeer, snowy owl

en.q: In the tundra biome people live in
options: igloos in winter and tents in summer
mud huts throughout the whole year
en.explanation: Tundra regions are also called barren lands; net primary productivity is very low.

ta.q: தூந்திரப் பகுதி மக்கள் குளிர்காலத்தில் வாழும் வீடுகள்

questions.quote: Freshwater biome: comprises lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, wetlands... Marine biomes are the largest aquatic biomes on earth... Coral reefs are a second kind of marine biomes... Estuaries form a third unique marine biome.

en.q: Which are the largest aquatic biomes on earth?
en.explanation: Marine biomes include oceans, coral reefs and estuaries.

ta.explanation: பெருங்கடல், பவளத்திட்டு, ஓதப்பொங்கு முகம் ஆகியவை கடல் தொகுதிகள்.

questions.quote: Some of the threats and issues to aquatic biomes are overfishing, pollution and rise in sea level. A Biosphere Reserve is a special ecosystem... There are 18 Biosphere Reserves in India.

en.q: Which of the following is a threat to aquatic biomes mentioned in the textbook?
en.explanation: Others are pollution and rise in sea level.
